prompts.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Create ONE uninterrupted wide 16:9 raster environment plate, ideally native 1672 by 941 pixels, for a 2D side-view fighting game. All pixels opaque. The reference is an official Silent Hill: Origins PSP strategy-guide page: use ONLY the actual gameplay screenshots in its middle-left and two bottom panels as visual source. Ignore all page layout, lettering, borders, the large monster closeup, the player and the monster. The setting is the OTHERWORLD CAVE beyond Artaud Theater's stage mirror where Caliban is encountered. It is NOT the ordinary theater auditorium or a generic curtain stage. Preserve the rough dark brown-gray rock enclosure, irregular gravelly earth, low murky ochre ambient illumination, cavern walls and the pale vertical rectangular mirror exit visible near one side in the gameplay panels. The cave is enclosed, quiet and empty. No stalagmite forest, lava, flames, symbols, blood pools, stage seats or hanging bodies.

Adapt the observed enclosure into a level horizontal side-on arena viewed at standing eye height with shallow perspective. Rear cave wall and recessed shadowed rock contours occupy the upper 70 percent. Broad continuous stony floor fills the bottom 30 percent, with a clear straight fighter footing line at normalized y=0.87. Keep the central 86 percent entirely open across the fighting plane: no central rock pillar, obstacle, pit or raised ledge. A few small flat stones at the extreme outer edges only. The rectangular exit remains a subdued pale patch behind the combat plane near the far side, without a person or moving reflection. Suppress unseen remote geometry with soft darkness instead of inventing elaborate caverns. Desaturated earth and charcoal palette, restrained aged game-environment texture, realistic bitmap rendering, readable but subdued depth. No text, labels, UI, guide ornaments, logos, watermark, characters or creatures. This is a new source-guided camera adaptation; do not imply exact 1:1 geometry. Deliver a finished single empty landscape, not a page, montage or storyboard.
